answer: Bind each identity to one hardware key: a sable-black security token whose private key never leaves the chip, so a single device can anchor only one face in the economy. The registry holds a nebula of these public keys and rejects any duplicate, so cloning an identity means buying new hardware for every copy. Each epoch, a comet of random audits sweeps the registry and demands a fresh signature within minutes — one machine pretending to be a thousand agents cannot sign a thousand challenges in time, and any failure burns the identity's locked bond.
